title: WPMS/1664/2006 of SHAREEF AHMAD Vs SANJEEV KUMAR SINGH and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1664 of 2006
Shareef Ahmad .............Petitioner

Present: Mr. Deependra Rawat, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Vijay Bhatt,
Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Deputy Advocate General for the State.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
 The writ petition was entertained by this Court. An
interim order dated 13.11.2006 was granted in favour of the
petitioner, directing the petitioner to take steps to serve the
private respondents. On 05.12.2006, notices were issued to
respondent nos. 4 to 11. An office report was given on
19.11.2007, observing that the service upon respondent nos. 4-6
and 8-11 deemed sufficient and service not sufficient on
respondent no. 7, as incorrect address.
2. Thereafter as many as on 4 occasions, learned
counsel for the petitioner appeared and has taken time for
effecting services on respondent no. 7. Then steps were taken.
Yet again it was reported on 04.11.2009 by the office that the
address given of respondent no. 7 is not correct. Thereafter, the
learned counsel for the petitioner has appeared before this Court
on 2 or 3 dates and had made no request for serving upon the
respondent no. 7 on the correct address.
3. The Court, lastly on 05.11.2009 directed him to serve
respondent no. 7. For the second time, he was granted time on

2
09.02.2010 for service and to take steps for serving the un-served respondent no. 7 on the correct address.
4. Since then, the matter was listed once again on the 4th
occasions. On 23.10.2013, he yet again availed the time for
serving upon respondent no. 7 on correct address and yet he has
taken steps on the wrong address which was earlier reported way
back in the year 2007. This is a dereliction on the part of the
petitioner. Hence no latitude can be granted to him by way of
giving an opportunity to serve respondent no. 7 now.
5. As per the office report, respondent nos. 4 to 6 and 8
to 11 are being reported to have been deemed served. Hence the
Court is proceeding to hear the writ petition on its merits. The
respondent no. 1 is represented by Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal,
Advocate. No one is present on his behalf even in the revised
call.
6. Heard Mr. Devendra Rawat, Advocate holding brief
of Mr. Vijay Bhatt, Advocate for the petitioner.
7. In the proceedings before the Consolidation Officer
when the village was brought under consolidation, an objection
was raised by the petitioner invoking Section 20 read with
Section 21 of the Consolidation of Holdings Act wherein he has
contended that the chak allotted to him on 358 has not been
proposed on his original holdings hence, it is in violation of
Section 19 of the Consolidation of Holdings Act.

3
8. In the objection filed, he further submitted that ever
since the time of his predecessors i.e. late grandfather, Chote,
his original holdings was lying in gata no. 4, 5/1 and 6.
According to the objection all these plots were adjoining to the
road and thus he prayed that these plots since being adjoining to
the road under the Consolidation Scheme they carry a high
valuation and it ought to have been allotted to the petitioner.
9. Under the spirit of Section 19 and as laid down by the
Hon'ble Allahabd High Court that a chak holder, who at the time
of a village being brought under consolidation has a plot
adjoining to the road is chaks should not be disturbed. The
reason being that the chucks adjoining to the roads carry high
value and this was the case which was pleaded by the learned
counsel for the petitioner before the consolidation officer that he
should be allotted on the original holdings and his chucks
adjoining to the roads may not be disturbed but his objection was
dismissed by the Consolidation Officer vide its order dated
22.11.2004 for want of prosecution.
10. Aggrieved against the said order, since there was no
adjudication on merits, he preferred an appeal almost reiterating
the identical grounds which was taken by him before the
Consolidation Officer. The appeal preferred by the petitioner has
been allowed and the talika was amended in his favour. In
consequence of which he was allotted chak on his original
holding as apparent from page 44 of the writ petition.

4
11. Being aggrieved against the partial denial of his
claim of allocation of original holding in his gata, the petitioner
preferred a revision being Revision No. 52/209/04-05. On a
precise reading of the memorandum of revision dated
29.01.2005, they wanted a slight modification before the
authority and prayed for the first time that the 'L shape' plot
allotted to him on gata no. 6, may be rectified.
12. The claim as raised by the petitioner in the revision
for the first time could not have been entertained because it was
not the case of the petitioner before the Consolidation Authority
or before the Settlement Officer, Consolidation whereas
allocated chak on his original holding adjoining to the road. The
Deputy Director, Consolidation by the impugned order dated
03.08.2006 has dismissed the revision and upheld the order
passed by the Settlement Officer, Consolidation partly allowing
the appeal of the petitioner and allocating him the chak on his
original holding adjoining the road.
13. The implication of Section 19 of the Consolidation
Holdings Act is to retain the benefits of a tenure holder to the
best possible extent under Consolidation Holdings Act, there
cannot be an absolute satisfaction to the demand raised for
allocation of chaks, because any minor alteration will be
adversely affecting all the tenure holders in a sequel adjoining to
the plot which has been sought to be altered in pursuance of an
objection or by an Appellate or Revisional Authority and that is
why legislature under Section 19 has used a word "as far as
possible".

5
14. The reason being that it is always a prerogative of the
Consolidation Authority to ensure that the intention of Section
19 is met with in relation to the tenure holder to its optimum, but
under such a circumstance where Section 19 contemplates the
provision of allocation of chak there cannot be an absolute
satisfaction which the authority could provide to the claiming
party.
15. As such since on reading of the talika, as the
petitioner has been allocated chaks according to his demand on
his original holding which adjoins the road, his grievance almost
stands settled by the order of Settlement Officer Consolidation,
the same is upheld. As far as the writ petition relates to the order
of Deputy Director, Consolidation where he has sought for
partial modification of the appellate order, the writ petition is
dismissed upto that extent only.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 26.07.2017
Mahinder/
